\section[profesional]{profesional — professional}

\label{lesson:ES-C475-profesional}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to deduct, then the Spanish for the blow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: profesional}
\textbf{profesional} — \textquotedblleft{}professional\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Buscamos un equipo profesional.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are looking for a professional team.}
\end{quote}

It is an adjective and a noun: \emph{un profesional} is a professional, a person who does the job for a living.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{profesional}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{profesional}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{profesional}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to deduct, then the Spanish for the blow, then say \emph{profesional} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does profesional mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Professional\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[el título]{el título — the qualification, the title}

\label{lesson:ES-C475-titulo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for professional, then the Spanish for initiative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el título}
\textbf{el título} — \textquotedblleft{}the qualification, the title\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es necesario el título de bachillerato.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The secondary-school qualification is required.}
\end{quote}

On a job notice \emph{el título} is a qualification; on a book it is the title.

One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
